title: Client Balance Tracking Corruption via Recipient Parameter Mismatch in withdraw()
description: The withdraw() function uses the `recipient` parameter to lookup and decrement clientBalances instead of msg.sender. This allows any authorized client to corrupt another client's balance tracking, locking them out of their funds. Note: The funds go to the specified recipient (victim), not to the attacker, making this a DoS/griefing attack rather than direct theft.
rootCause: The withdraw() function uses the `recipient` parameter to lookup clientBalances instead of msg.sender, allowing any authorized client to corrupt another client's balance accounting
impact: Any authorized client can zero out another client's balance tracking, effectively locking them out of future withdrawals. While the underlying funds are not stolen (DOLA goes to the victim/recipient), the accounting corruption prevents normal operations.
attackPath: Client B (also authorized) calls withdraw(token, 1000, clientA) with Client A's address as recipient
DOLA is redeemed and sent to clientA (the recipient/victim)
Client A cannot withdraw because their tracked balance shows 0, despite receiving the DOLA
recommendation: Change the balance lookup to use msg.sender instead of recipient. The recipient parameter should only be used for determining where to send the withdrawn funds, not for determining whose balance to debit.
